# Why and With Whom

This part asks why an analysis should be reproducible at all, and
what an analyst owes to the collaborators who depend on the work.
It is the first part of the first quarter, and it is deliberately
light on code; the chapters that follow supply the tools, and these
supply the reasons for using them. (De-identification and the
obligations an analyst owes to the participants whose records make
the work possible move, in this volume, to the Compliance and
Ethics part of Volume 3.)

- @sec-why distinguishes methods, results, and inferential
  reproducibility, and names the check that makes each common
  failure loud.
- @sec-team-science runs the intake conversation, places an
  engagement on the collaboration spectrum, and settles authorship.

Each chapter opens with a short 'Skip ahead?' quiz. If the quiz at
the start of a chapter is easy, skip to the next chapter; if it is
not, the chapter is written for you.
